thread:
Elaine: heads-up — started a quick spike on exporter routing for tenant-tiered retention. idea: primary export to Tempo for traces, fallback to Honeycomb only for high-sample debugging tenants. want to avoid duplicating high-cardinality events into HC for all tenants.
Max: makes sense. current problem is Datadog customers expect spans there too. how do we decide routing vs fanout? cost explosion if we fanout everywhere.
Sam: proposal: routing policy based on tenant metadata + route table in our control plane. simple rules: tenant.retention == "hot" -> fanout: tempo + datadog; tenant.retention == "debug" -> tempo + honeycomb; else tempo-only. keep fanout bounded with per-tenant quotas.
Priya: +1. need to ensure exporter-level backpressure doesn't blow up CPU when datadog is slow. suggest circuit-breaker per-exporter + adaptive batching.
Ian: Also add a traffic-weighted rollout flag so we can A/B the new routing policy via console (rollout %). we need metrics: exports/s, errors/s, queue_length per exporter.
Elaine: agreed. small checklist I started:
- control-plane routing table proto (tenant_id -> route_policy)
- exporter adapters: tempo, datadog, honeycomb (with per-tenant rate limiter)
- per-exporter circuit-breaker and retry budget
- console UX: rollout toggle + route inspection for a tenant
- alerts: exporter error rate + export queue depth
Max: for proto, what fields do we need? tenant_id, retention_tier, allowed_backends, max_tokens_per_min? maybe sampling_hint.
Sam: keep it minimal for v1: tenant_id, retention_tier, allowed_backends (list), sampling_override (p99 tracer only). we can compute quotas from tenant contract.
Priya: implementation notes — our otel-collector config will need a route processor. pseudoconfig:
```yaml
processors:
  tenantrouter:
    table:
      - tenant: abc
        backends: [tempo, datadog]
      - tenant: acme-debug
        backends: [tempo, honeycomb]
exporters:
  tempo:
    endpoint: https://tempo.int.redwood/api/v1/otlp
  honeycomb:
    endpoint: https://api.honeycomb.io/otlp/v1
  datadog:
    endpoint: https://api.datadoghq.com/api/v2/otlp
service:
  pipelines:
    traces:
      processors: [tenantrouter, batch]
      exporters: [] # dynamically set by tenantrouter
```
Priya: tenantrouter would mutate the pipeline to forward to the chosen exporters and attach a header with tenant-id and retention.
Ian: How do we handle retention/TTL differences? Tempo has short TTL per table, Honeycomb needs dataset mapping. We should surface dataset name in the route and a retention hint header so downstream infra can store accordingly.
Elaine: agree — add route.metadata.dataset and route.metadata.retention_hint. also we need a migration for existing private customers who push straight to datadog; don't break API keys.
Max: auth problem: some tenants provide hosted datadog API keys. we can't centrally rewrite those into our datadog exporter unless we store keys. storing tenant keys is ok but must be encrypted in KMS. add to security checklist.
Sam: got it. I'll add KMS encryption and access policy to the ticket.
Priya: testing plan: unit tests for router table, e2e with a small local otel-collector and synthetic traces that assert the exporter receives correct headers. quick test command I used:
```
# send a single span with tenant header
otel-cli span --name "test-route" --attr tenant.id=acme-debug --endpoint http://localhost:4318/v1/traces
```
Elaine: deployed a tiny canary: tenantrouter v1 -> 5% of tenants. deploy-bot: canary deploy started.
deploy-bot: Canary rollout started for tenantrouter v1: 5% target, 12 pods -> 1 pod with new image. logs will stream to #eng-platform.
Max: saw one failure in logs, exporter honeycomb 429 on test tenant. is our retry budget too low?
Priya: that 429 was expected for the test dataset (rate limit). circuit-breaker tripped, router fell back to tempo only — good. we need to surface this fallback event in traces/console so SEs know their requested fanout didn't occur.
Ian: console UX idea: when a tenant is selected, show last 24h route decisions + fallback reasons (rate_limit, auth_fail, exporter_down). small timeline widget.
Elaine: also add an admin endpoint to re-run routing evaluation for a tenant (useful for debugging) and a way to temporarily force fanout for a tenant for 1h.
Sam: note: be careful with 'force fanout' — must be audited and limited by role. add audit logs to action.
Priya: also record per-tenant spool metrics to measure downstream backlog: per-tenant queued_spans, max_queue_age, last_export_error.
Max: for storage impact analysis, we should simulate 30-day retention hot tenants at expected qps and estimate bytes/day to each vendor. I'll run a load sim and share numbers.
Elaine: cool. timeline: aim for small beta (control-plane + adapters) in 2 weeks, console bits in 3. canaries at 5% -> 25% -> 100% over a week each stage.
Ian: I'll draft the console wireframe and share in #design later.
Sam: creating a GH epic: infra/telemetry/tenant-routing. assigning tasks: router proto (me), otel-collector adapter (Priya), exporter circuit-breakers (Max), console work (Ian), security/KMS (Elaine/Sam).
Priya: added a note: watch out for span attribute cardinality when routing to honeycomb — we should scrub or limit attributes for honeycomb datasets to avoid high cardinality costs.
Elaine: great catch. let's default to attribute allowlist for vendor-specific exports and expose per-tenant overrides behind an admin flag.
Max: 👍
Sam: will open the epic now and add subtasks + acceptance criteria.
Elaine: thanks all. if anyone wants to test locally ping me for the canary image and otel-collector config.
Ian: pinged design. will sync tomorrow.
Priya: one more: add alert severity mapping. exporter errors for enterprise tenants -> P1, for free-tier -> P3.
Elaine: noted. end of thread.
